title: Composables: reusable behavior without hidden global state
outcome: Extract reactive behavior with explicit inputs, lifecycle cleanup, and a predictable return API.
useCase: Selection, pagination, subscriptions, and reusable editor behavior.
drawbacks: Hidden singleton state and implicit dependencies can make bugs travel.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Inputs visible. State owned. Effects cleaned up.

trace.title: Explicit input
trace.detail: A composable is a function that packages reusable stateful logic. It is not simply any helper with use in its name. A pure formatter is often just a function.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Two components call useSelection. Each call allocates one ref, so they can select different tickets. Move the ref above the function and both callers now share it. Neither version is automatically better; the intended ownership decides.

Test composables with pure seams when possible. For lifecycle-dependent behavior, mount a small component and verify listeners are removed when it unmounts.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Creating a timer without clearing it can keep updating a vanished view. A composable that silently reads route, store, and global user state is harder to reuse than one with explicit dependencies.
